exploration.title: Orbit Workshop
exploration.subject: Physics
exploration.summary: Compare collisions, orbits and escapes by changing one launch variable at a time.
exploration.question: How does sideways launch speed change a falling path?
exploration.explanation: Gravity accelerates a probe toward the central body while sideways motion carries it forward. At one starting radius in this model, too little sideways speed intersects the drawn surface, the baseline speed makes a circular orbit, and at least √2 times that baseline escapes. Doubling central mass raises the circular speed to √2 times the original baseline, so an unchanged launch curves into a tighter ellipse. Gravity continues to act along bound and escape paths.

experiments.title: Change only sideways speed
experiments.instruction: Predict the outcome order at 0.60×, 1.00× and 1.42× speed. Keep central mass at 1× and starting distance fixed, then compare all three paths.
experiments.observe: The paths collide, orbit and escape in that order. Gravity still curves the escaping path.

experiments.title: Change only central mass
experiments.instruction: Predict the path at 2× central mass. Keep launch speed at 1.00× and starting distance fixed, then compare with 1× mass.
experiments.observe: The 1×-mass path stays near circular; the 2×-mass path becomes a tighter ellipse because circular speed is higher.

exploration.misconception: Escape does not mean gravity switches off. Gravity weakens with distance and keeps curving the escape path even though it cannot turn the probe back.
